title: Session-usage collection fix

conformance.reason: Task 26.5 replaces the opencode-CLI dependency in the orchestrator's session-usage collector with a direct HTTP request. It depends on no unverified Jellyfin or provider behavior, changes no product behavior, and implements no ADR clause. No pre-dispatch specialist conformance check applies.

notes: collect-session-usage.sh now fetches /api/session/<id> directly: curl -fsS --max-time 60 preferred, with a pure-bash /dev/tcp HTTP/1.0 fallback when curl is absent; the OPENCODE_SERVER override and the opencode serve --port discovery are unchanged, and the opencode CLI is no longer on the success path. The jq extraction and output contract are byte-identical to the pre-change script (verified for two real sessions, including with the CLI absent and with the curl-less fallback).

The running server enforces HTTP basic auth; the script sends credentials as user 'opencode' with OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD when set. The reviewer's security check confirmed no password, base64 credential, or Authorization header reaches stdout/stderr/a file on any path, including caller-forced bash -x, because api_get's stderr is redirected and the fallback writes the header on fd 3 (stdin to base64, not argv); curl masks the -u value in /proc/<pid>/cmdline and ps.

Carried informational notes (none blocking): R1 the /dev/tcp fallback has no request timeout (a hang, never a wrong figure; the pre-change explicit-server branch was also unbounded); R2 a >76-column base64 header wrap would still fail closed with the documented error; R3 the curl -u credential sits in argv, bounded by curl's scrubbing.
